question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A story intended to teach moral lessons
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Parable"** means a simple story used to illustrate a moral or spiritual lesson. (नीतिकथा)

 
 
• **Example:** The **parable** of the Good Samaritan teaches us the importance of helping others in need.
 
• **Example**: My life felt like a** parable** of the rewards of hard work.
 
 

Hence, we can infer that the correct answer for a story intended to teach moral lessons is **'Parable'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Parboil** (अधपका करना): To partially cook food by boiling it briefly.

 
 
• **Example:** You should** parboil **the carrots before adding them to the stew.
 
 
 
• **Parole** (परोल): The temporary or permanent release of a prisoner before the expiry of a sentence, on the promise of good behavior.
 
 
• **Example:** He was released on** parole** after serving ten years of his sentence.
 
 
 
• **Parasite** (परजीवी): An organism that lives in or on another organism and benefits by deriving nutrients at the host's expense.
 
 
• **Example:** The** parasite **attaches itself to the host and feeds off its nutrients.
